backlog.title: PRD Divergence Remediation — pi-mulligan v1.1 Nudge/Audit/Guard Layer
backlog.description: Remediate the 4 PRD divergences found in the pi-mulligan v1.1 validation pass. All 4 are in the nudge/audit/guard layer — none affect core soft-delete correctness or cause data loss. The core rewind/shrink/cancel/checkpoint/banner mechanisms are verified correct (1042 tests pass). Fixes: BUG-001 (driftThresholdTokens reconciliation), BUG-002 (high-water nudge awareness-only text), BUG-003 (audit report checkpoint annotation), BUG-004 (rewind depth guard cancel-exclusion). Research findings stored in plan/007_67d7d8c6e4c5/bugfix/001_8fe6022f172a/architecture/.

milestones.title: Major Bug Fixes — driftThresholdTokens reconciliation + high-water nudge awareness-only
milestones.description: Fix the 2 Major-severity divergences. BUG-001: reconcile the driftThresholdTokens default (research shows code and spec/09 already agree at 4000 with >=; the remaining issue is the stale > text in spec/07 §5.1 and deviation framing). BUG-002: rewrite renderHighWaterNudge to be awareness-only per PRD §5.2 v1.1 note ('pure awareness, not rewind/shrink'), because the signal fires on total context including user pastes whose content the agent cannot legitimately shed.

tasks.title: BUG-001 — Reconcile driftThresholdTokens default (4000 + >=) with spec consistency
tasks.description: The PRD claims spec/09 specifies driftThresholdTokens: 6000, but research confirms the current spec/09 §2 and §3 ALREADY show 4000 with the rationale 'Lowered from 6000 with the comparison changed from > to >=' (the spec was amended in a prior fix cycle). The code (config.ts:168) and config.test.ts:30,64 already assert 4000. The ONLY remaining inconsistency is spec/07 §5.1 text still using strict > while code and spec/09 use >=. Fix that text and clean up 'deviation' framing. This is a reconciliation/consistency task, not a value change.

subtasks.title: Fix spec/07 §5.1 stale > operator to >= and clean up deviation framing in nudges.ts
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/007_67d7d8c6e4c5/bugfix/001_8fe6022f172a/architecture/bug_analysis.md §BUG-001. The PRD's claim that 'spec/09 specifies 6000' is STALE — the current spec/09 §2 (line 45) and §3 (line 84) ALREADY show 4000 with rationale 'Lowered from 6000 with the comparison changed from > to >='. The code (src/config.ts:168), config.test.ts:30, and config.test.ts:64 all already assert/expect 4000. The code comparison operator at src/nudges.ts:332 is already >=. There is NO value change needed. The remaining work is textual consistency only.
2. INPUT: The current spec/07-preventive-and-nudges.md §5.1 (line 170) text reads 'avg(window.deltaTokens) > driftThresholdTokens' using strict >. This contradicts spec/09 §3's documented >= change and the code at src/nudges.ts:332 ('return avg >= config.nudges.driftThresholdTokens'). The nudges.ts comment block at lines 297-306 frames this as a 'SPEC-AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION' / 'BUG-003 fix' deviation.
3. LOGIC: (a) In spec/07-preventive-and-nudges.md §5.1, change the textual comparison operator from strict '>' to '>=' to match spec/09 §3 and the code (this is a 1-character spec-text fix that closes the last spec-internal inconsistency). (b) In src/nudges.ts, update the comment block at lines 297-306 to reference spec/09 §3 as the authority for the >= operator rather than framing it as a 'resolution' of an ambiguity — the spec now codifies >= explicitly. Keep the mathematical worked examples (they are correct and valuable). (c) Verify that config.test.ts already asserts driftThresholdTokens: 4000 (it does at lines 13-30 and 64) and that drift_nudge.test.ts:128-143 tests the >= behavior at 4000 (they do) — NO test changes needed; just confirm they pass.
4. OUTPUT: spec/07 §5.1 text is internally consistent with spec/09 §3 and the code (all say >=). nudges.ts comment no longer implies 4000 is a 'deviation' from spec. All 1042 existing tests still pass (no behavioral change).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The spec/07 text fix and nudges.ts comment cleanup ride WITH this work. The README (line 98) already documents 4000 with >= correctly — no change needed. No separate docs subtask for this subtask.

tasks.title: BUG-002 — Rewrite high-water nudge to awareness-only (no rewind/shrink prescription)
tasks.description: renderHighWaterNudge (src/nudges.ts:534-543) prescribes mulligan_rewind/mulligan_shrink ('Consider mulligan_shrink or mulligan_rewind to reclaim space'). The PRD spec/07 §5.2 v1.1 note (D10 amendment) explicitly states the high-water signal's 'prescription is pure awareness, not rewind/shrink.' This is load-bearing: the high-water signal measures TOTAL filtered context (including user content) and fires on large user pastes — prescribing rewind/shrink on user-attributable bloat is misaligned because the guardrail (spec/13 §1) protects user messages from rewind and shrinking ground-truth input is wrong. Rewrite both text paths (percentage + fallback) to be awareness-only.

subtasks.title: Rewrite renderHighWaterNudge text to awareness-only, update JSDoc, update tests, update README quote
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/007_67d7d8c6e4c5/bugfix/001_8fe6022f172a/architecture/bug_analysis.md §BUG-002. The function renderHighWaterNudge is at src/nudges.ts:534-543 (EXPORTED). It has TWO return paths: (a) percentage path (line 540): returns `[mulligan] Context is at ~${pct}% of the window. Consider mulligan_shrink or mulligan_rewind to reclaim space.` (b) fallback for windowTokens <= 0 (line 538): returns `[mulligan] Context is filling up. Consider mulligan_shrink or mulligan_rewind to reclaim space.` BOTH must stop prescribing rewind/shrink. The JSDoc at lines 520-522 says 'recommends mulligan_shrink/mulligan_rewind' and must be updated. The function is PURE (never throws), retains the [mulligan] prefix + rounded percentage (Math.round), and is ~25-40 tokens. The injectHighWaterNudge function (line 555+) calls renderHighWaterNudge and wraps the result — NO CHANGE to the injection mechanism, only the text content changes.
2. INPUT: The percentage is computed as `Math.round((totalFilteredTokens / windowTokens) * 100)`. The PRD spec/07 §5.2 v1.1 note (line 172) states: 'its prescription is pure awareness, not rewind/shrink.' The rationale: the high-water signal fires on TOTAL filtered context (including user pastes per spec/10 §2.1 F-drift-userexempt), so prescribing rewind/shrink on user-attributable bloat is misaligned — the guardrail (spec/13 §1) protects user messages from rewind.
3. LOGIC: Rewrite BOTH return paths of renderHighWaterNudge to be awareness-only. (a) Percentage path: retain `[mulligan]` prefix + `~${pct}% of the window` but replace the prescription with an awareness suggestion, e.g. `[mulligan] Context is at ~${pct}% of the window; review recent output for reclaimable space.` (b) Fallback: `[mulligan] Context is filling up; review recent output for reclaimable space.` The text MUST NOT contain the strings 'mulligan_rewind' or 'mulligan_shrink'. Update the JSDoc comment (lines 520-522) to say the text is awareness-only per spec/07 §5.2 v1.1 note. Then update test assertions: in test/drift_nudge.test.ts the describe block 'renderHighWaterNudge — one-line annotation' (around line 486): change the test that asserts output contains 'mulligan_shrink' (line 495) and 'mulligan_rewind' (line 496) to instead assert the text does NOT contain those tool names and DOES contain the percentage + '[mulligan]'. Change the fallback test (around line 506-510) that asserts 'mulligan_shrink' to assert awareness-only text without tool names. The rounding tests (line 499: ~75%, ~67%) and the filter.test.ts:955-967 test (asserts ~70%) need NO change. TDD: write the failing assertions first (they assert the new text), then change the code to pass.
4. OUTPUT: renderHighWaterNudge returns awareness-only text in both paths. All tests pass. The string 'mulligan_rewind' and 'mulligan_shrink' do NOT appear in the high-water nudge output.
5. MOCKING: renderHighWaterNudge is a pure function — no Pi mocking needed. The filter.test.ts integration tests use a fake Pi (makePi/makeCtx) but only assert on customType and percentage, not the prescription text — no mock changes needed.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Update README.md line 233 which currently quotes the exact old nudge text: '[mulligan] Context is at ~70% of the window. Consider mulligan_shrink or mulligan_rewind to reclaim space.' — replace the quoted text with the new awareness-only example. This rides WITH the work (the subtask touches this exact README quote).

milestones.title: Minor Bug Fixes — audit checkpoint annotation + rewind depth guard cancel-exclusion
milestones.description: Fix the 2 Minor-severity divergences. BUG-003: add the required '(user-set)' annotation to the audit report checkpoint clause (spec/13 §4 step 3) and singularize the count. BUG-004: update countRewindMarkers to exclude cancelled markers, mirroring the BUG-005 cancel-exclusion pattern already in countRetriesAtLatestPrompt, so the depth guard honors spec/05 §1 step 4 'count active' and the cancel-then-retry workflow is not blocked.

tasks.title: BUG-003 — Add '(user-set)' annotation to audit report checkpoint clause + singularize count
tasks.description: renderAuditReport (src/tools/audit.ts:448-454) renders the checkpoint clause as 'N checkpoints [names]' without the '(user-set)' annotation required by spec/13 §4 step 3, and does not singularize '1 checkpoints' to '1 checkpoint'. This affects both the agent mulligan_audit tool and the human /mulligan_audit command (shared renderer). The '(user-set)' annotation is meaningful in v1.1 because checkpoints moved to the user (E23) — it distinguishes them as user-owned destructive-power grants.

subtasks.title: Update renderAuditReport checkpoint clause: add '(user-set)', singularize count, update all affected tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/007_67d7d8c6e4c5/bugfix/001_8fe6022f172a/architecture/bug_analysis.md §BUG-003. The renderAuditReport function is at src/tools/audit.ts:440-480 (EXPORTED). The checkpoint clause is built around line 453: `${args.checkpointNames.length} checkpoints${ckptNames}${cancelledClause}` where ckptNames is ` [name1, name2]` or ` []`. spec/13 §4 step 3 (line 89) requires: 'N checkpoints [names] (user-set)'. The function is PURE and shared by the agent tool and the human command (spec/13 §4 'same renderer').
2. INPUT: args.checkpointNames is a string[] (the active checkpoint names). When length > 0, the current output is 'N checkpoints [name1, name2]'. When length === 0, it is '0 checkpoints []'.
3. LOGIC: Update the checkpoint clause rendering in renderAuditReport: (a) Singularize: use 'checkpoint' (singular) when args.checkpointNames.length === 1, 'checkpoints' (plural) otherwise (including 0). (b) Add '(user-set)' annotation: when args.checkpointNames.length > 0, append ' (user-set)' after the names bracket; when length === 0, omit it (nothing is armed). Example outputs: '2 checkpoints [before-x, before-y] (user-set)', '1 checkpoint [solo] (user-set)', '0 checkpoints []'. The cancelledClause (', N cancelled (retired)') goes AFTER the (user-set) annotation — verify ordering. Then update all affected tests: test/tools/audit.test.ts line 550 (append ' (user-set)' to the 2-checkpoint assertion), line 929 (same), line 975 ('0 checkpoints []' stays unchanged — no annotation when 0). Add a NEW test asserting singular: checkpointNames:['solo'] renders '1 checkpoint [solo] (user-set)'. The commands.test.ts buildExpectedReport() at line 538 calls renderAuditReport with checkpointNames:[] (no checkpoints in its fixtures) so it is unaffected — verify this. The test at audit.test.ts:580 dynamically finds the 'Active markers:' line and checks 'cancelled (retired)' — verify it still works with the (user-set) annotation present.
4. OUTPUT: renderAuditReport checkpoint clause includes '(user-set)' when checkpoints exist and singularizes the count. All tests pass.
5. MOCKING: renderAuditReport is a pure function — no Pi mocking needed for the renderer tests. The full-pipeline tests use fake ctx (makeCtx with entries) — no mock changes needed.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] No user-facing/config/API surface change beyond the audit report text format. No README change needed for this subtask (the audit report format is not quoted verbatim in the README). The changeset-level docs task (P1.M3.T1) will sweep README if needed.

tasks.title: BUG-004 — Exclude cancelled markers from rewind depth guard (countRewindMarkers)
tasks.description: countRewindMarkers (src/tools/rewind.ts:204-220) counts ALL mulligan:rewind entries without excluding those retired by a mulligan:cancel, contradicting spec/05 §1 step 4 'count active.' The sibling countRetriesAtLatestPrompt ALREADY excludes cancelled rewinds (BUG-005 fix), making the two guards internally inconsistent. An agent that creates 5 rewinds, cancels all 5 (0 active), and attempts a 6th is incorrectly refused with a misleading '5 active rewind marker(s)' message, blocking the cancel-then-retry workflow.

subtasks.title: Add cancel-exclusion to countRewindMarkers, fix stale comments, add cancel-then-retry regression test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/007_67d7d8c6e4c5/bugfix/001_8fe6022f172a/architecture/bug_analysis.md §BUG-004. The countRewindMarkers function is at src/tools/rewind.ts:204-220 (module-private, tested indirectly via tool behavior). It currently scans ALL entries for type==='custom' && customType==='mulligan:rewind' and returns the count — NEVER checking for mulligan:cancel entries. Its stale comment (line 199-203) says 'Markers are permanent (never cleared), so ALL persisted rewind markers count toward maxDepth' — this is pre-E21 reasoning; markers ARE now retractable via mulligan_cancel. The EXACT pattern to mirror is in countRetriesAtLatestPrompt (rewind.ts:270-340, the BUG-005 fix): it scans for mulligan:cancel entries, collects data.targetId into a Set<string> (cancelledRewindIds), then skips any mulligan:rewind whose data.id is in that Set. IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE: countRewindMarkers scans the ENTIRE entry list (cumulative depth guard), so the cancel scan must also cover ALL entries (not just post-latest-prompt like countRetriesAtLatestPrompt does). The depth guard is called at rewind.ts:525. The refusal text at line 528 reports '${depth} active rewind marker(s)' — with the fix, depth will correctly exclude cancelled markers. The filter.ts readMarkers cancelledIds mechanism (filter.ts:101-205) is the canonical version of this pattern.
2. INPUT: ctx.sessionManager.getEntries() returns the full entry list. Entries with type==='custom' && customType==='mulligan:rewind' are rewind markers (data.id is the uuid). Entries with type==='custom' && customType==='mulligan:cancel' are cancel entries (data.targetId is the uuid of the retired marker). A rewind is ACTIVE iff its data.id is NOT in the set of cancelled targetIds.
3. LOGIC: (a) In countRewindMarkers, add a FIRST pass over ALL entries to collect mulligan:cancel data.targetId values into a Set<string> (cancelledRewindIds). Read targetId defensively: typeof string && length > 0. Wrap each entry access in try/catch (never throw — E13). (b) In the SECOND pass (the existing rewind count loop), skip any mulligan:rewind entry whose data.id (read defensively) is in cancelledRewindIds. A rewind with an unreadable/missing data.id is COUNTED (conservative: never exclude on bad data — matches countRetriesAtLatestPrompt's polarity). (c) Update the stale comment at lines 199-203: remove 'Markers are permanent (never cleared)' and explain cancelled markers are excluded per spec/05 §1 step 4 'count active' (reference the E21 cancel mechanism and the BUG-005 sibling fix in countRetriesAtLatestPrompt). (d) Update the depth-guard comment at line 524 ('Markers are permanent → ALL persisted rewind markers count toward maxDepth') to reflect the cancel-exclusion. (e) Add a NEW regression test: build entries with 5 mulligan:rewind markers (each with a unique data.id) + 5 mulligan:cancel entries (each with data.targetId matching one rewind id) + a user message entry. Call makeRewindTool(pi).execute(...) with valid params → the rewind SUCCEEDS (0 active markers, depth guard passes). Use existing test helpers: customEntry() and rewindEntryData() from test/tools/rewind.test.ts. Build cancel entries as customEntry('mulligan:cancel', { targetId: 'rew-N' }). Mirror the structure of the BUG-005 cancel-exclusion test at rewind.test.ts:1133-1161. (f) Verify existing depth guard tests still pass: rewind.test.ts:404-412 (5 non-cancelled → refused), rewind.test.ts:418-428 (4 → succeeds), edge-cases.test.ts:438-446 (same boundary). These should be UNCHANGED because their fixtures have no cancel entries.
4. OUTPUT: countRewindMarkers returns the count of ACTIVE (non-cancelled) rewind markers. The cancel-then-retry workflow works: 5 cancelled rewinds → 6th succeeds. The refusal text accurately reports active (non-cancelled) count. All tests pass.
5. MOCKING: countRewindMarkers is tested indirectly via the tool's execute() path. Use the existing fake ctx (makeCtx with entries) and fake pi (makePi). No new mocks needed — the cancel entries are just additional SessionEntry objects in the entries array.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] No user-facing/config/API surface change. The refusal text format is unchanged (only the count value becomes accurate). No README change needed for this subtask.
